rulings.challenge_claim: The row's load-bearing evidence — a five-site set of 'says Yahweh'/'declares Yahweh' signatures — is a blended sweep across three distinct byte objects with no pointed splice anywhere, and one member is not a Yahweh signature at all in either witness.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes; OL's object analysis and every digit hold. The five cited sites resolve into THREE count-objects: (i) the adjacent verb-plus-tetragrammaton signature אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה closing MT 54:1, which stands at BYTE tier in exactly 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses, MT 39:6, 54:1, 65:25, 66:21, 66:23) and collates to tier NONE against each of oshb:Isa.54.6, oshb:Isa.54.8, oshb:Isa.54.10 and oshb:Isa.54.17; (ii) the suffixed God-noun variant אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ closing MT 54:6 — no tetragrammaton in the frame, and the row's own cited WEB rendering reads a your-God form at web:Isa.54.6 — the separate divine-speech variant the census keeps apart, here folded under a Yahweh label; (iii) the postpositive oracle signature נְאֻם יְהוָֽה closing MT 54:17, a different formula census entirely. Two further SHAPES sit inside object (i)'s family but are not the adjacent formula: אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (MT 54:8) and אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה (MT 54:10) each interpose a participial epithet. Zero of the five is spliced in the row. The blend is load-bearing, not incidental: the same set is the ground both for holding the whole chapter as one unit and for rejecting the finer cut in strongest_rejected_alternative, which names web:Isa.54.6 among the 'says Yahweh'/'declares Yahweh' signatures. HIGH severity confirmed. Second finding UPHELD with its object CORRECTED: OL rests the internal-onset point on the pivot token לֹ֣א, byte-identical at MT 54:1 and MT 54:11 — true, but that exact pointed form stands in 94 verses book-wide at byte tier, six of them inside this very chapter (MT 54:1, 54:4, 54:10, 54:11, 54:14, 54:17), so it discriminates nothing. The discriminating object is the four-token contour: רָנִּ֥י עֲקָרָ֖ה לֹ֣א יָלָ֑דָה (MT 54:1) and עֲנִיָּ֥ה סֹעֲרָ֖ה לֹ֣א נֻחָ֑מָה (MT 54:11) carry an IDENTICAL accent sequence — merkha, tipcha, munach, etnachta — over the same vocative-plus-negative-plus-qatal shape, and MT 54:1 is the row's own front-seam warrant. On that object the finding stands: an undisclosed internal vocative onset built on the row's own seam shape. But OL OVERSTATES its consequence: MT 54:11 addresses the SAME feminine addressee, so the row's 'no fresh addressee or scene shift' survives literally; the defect is non-disclosure of a live rival cut, not a false universal. Third UPHELD: a paseq seg stands at MT 54:2 in the single-witness inventory, inside the span and undisclosed, while the row's parashah set is complete and correctly typed (SAMEKH at MT 53:12, 54:8, 54:10, 54:17, petuchah never conflated) and the ketiv/qere at MT 54:16 is described exactly right — the unpointed ketiv running into the pointed qere as the doubled token pair הן הִנֵּ֤ה. So symmetry fails on the paseq layer alone. Fourth UPHELD: the cross-seam title claim is untiered — קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.54.5, byte tier, sweep: 3 verses at byte tier, MT 30:12, 31:1, 54:5) against the prefixed וְלִקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.55.5); the MT 54:5 run reaches only accent_stripped tier at MT 55:5, and the MT 55:5 form reaches tier NONE at MT 54:5, so 'a byte-true device' that 'recurs' breaches the tier-disclosure standard. rulings.grounds: Credit verified first: ה֤וֹי כָּל צָמֵא֙ reaches byte tier verse-initially at oshb:Isa.55.1 — that pointed form stands at byte tier in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse) against 21 verses accent-stripped — and the row names the role correctly as the invitation cry, neither a woe-oracle onset nor the divine self-exclamation, with the different lexeme not blended in. The first defect is UPHELD at bytes. MT 55:1-3 address a masculine PLURAL throughout — the imperative chain plus אָזְנְכֶם֙ and נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם at MT 55:3 — MT 55:4 carries no second-person form at all, and MT 55:5 turns to masculine SINGULAR across the whole verse: the verb תֵדַע֙ early, then אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ and the closing פֵאֲרָֽךְ. A singular-you suffix stands in exactly 1 of the 7 verses MT 55:1-55:7 and MT 55:5 is that verse — OL's digit re-derived and exact. Both witnesses render every one of these with the same undifferentiated English pronoun, so the turn lives only in the Hebrew; a row whose sole declared driver is the addressee shift, and which ends ON that verse, owes the disclosure. The second defect is UPHELD with a refinement that helps the row: דִּרְשׁ֥וּ at MT 55:6 (byte tier, sweep: 2 verses book-wide, MT 1:17 and MT 55:6) is the same masculine-plural imperative class already running inside the span — לְכ֣וּ at MT 55:1 and וּלְכ֣וּ at MT 55:3 alongside the other plural imperatives — so 'a further imperative' is not a form-class change and, with the form claim neutralised, the seam would rest on a tier-3 single-witness seg that can never drive. NEW FINDING neither primary made: the seam is not warrantless — what DOES change at MT 55:6 is the addressee NUMBER, back to masculine plural after the masculine singular of MT 55:5, which is a byte-real tier-1 warrant the row never states. One imprecision in OL's own citation: MT 55:3's attested token is the waw-prefixed form, not the bare imperative it names (the bare form is a substring of it). Third item UPHELD: the cross-seam title disclosure is unquoted and untiered on both sides — the prefixed MT 55:5 form is not byte-identical to the MT 54:5 title and reaches accent-stripped tier only.

(c) device_notes: tier-label the title recurrence at accent-stripped tier with the prefixed MT 55:5 form spliced — the same edit ordered on the chapter-54 row, written in a distinct formulation per the variation order. rulings.challenge_claim: The row asserts that its governing frame recurs verbatim at byte tier between its two cited verses, and the bytes refuse it — the two forms differ in pointing, not merely accents, and reach only consonantal tier against each other.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived; OL is exactly right, including its diagnosis of the cause. The row's own splice כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה reaches byte tier at oshb:Isa.56.1 and collates against oshb:Isa.56.4 at SKELETON (consonantal) tier only, in both directions; the MT 56:4 form is כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה. It fails even the accent-stripped tier because the divergence is in the POINTING, not the accents: the opening letter carries a dagesh at MT 56:1 and none at MT 56:4, so accent-stripping cannot equalise the two. 'Recurs verbatim at byte tier' is therefore FALSE as written, and it is the row's stated ground for holding the whole span as one admission unit. A second respect in which the two are not one object: the MT 56:4 instance is not verse-initial — the verse opens כִּי, subordinating the frame, where MT 56:1 stands verse-initial. Added digit: the MT 56:1 pointed run stands at byte tier in exactly 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, MT 43:16, 56:1, 66:1). Second item UPHELD, scoped: נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה occupies the FIRST three tokens of MT 56:8 — verse-initial — and heads the gathering clause it is said to seal, and the WEB rendering likewise places the formula ahead of the quoted speech at web:Isa.56.8. The formula CLASS is postpositive book-wide, so the class label is not a fabrication; this INSTANCE is not postpositive, so 'closes on ... which seals' is a position claim the bytes refuse. Third item UPHELD: the byte-identical closing run shared by MT 55:13 and MT 56:5 straddles this row's front seam undisclosed here too (byte tier, sweep: 2 verses; skeleton 3 verses) — the same seam-pair edit ordered on the row ending at web:Isa.55.13. Fourth, OL's unused-unity point is byte-exact and is the evidence the row actually needs: שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ is BYTE-IDENTICAL at MT 56:2 and MT 56:6 (sweep: 2 verses, the only two in the book) and וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי is byte-identical at MT 56:4 and MT 56:6 (sweep: 2 verses) — a byte refrain pair bracketing the third-person turn the row argues across. Credit verified: frame ownership is right (both cited sites sit on the divine side, the four royal-messenger sites stay in the narrative zone); the MT 56:8 divine-name object is correctly named as the stacked title-plus-tetragrammaton form rather than the bare title; and mark handling is exact — SAMEKH at MT 56:2, 56:3 and 56:5 plus the front-seam seg at MT 55:13, petuchah never conflated, the MT 56:4 paseq disclosed count-only with no intra-verse position, and 0 ketiv/qere notes across MT 56:1-56:8. MY ADDITION: the row carries confidence HIGH, and the two supports it leans on hardest — the verbatim frame recurrence and the closing-formula position — are both byte-refuted, so the band itself is now unsupported and must be re-argued under the dependent-field rule, not merely re-worded. HIGH severity confirmed.
rulings.remedy: Author work order. (a) device_notes: replace 'recurs verbatim at byte tier' with the collate truth — the two frame runs match at SKELETON tier only, failing byte AND accent-stripped because of the dagesh difference on the opening letter, and the MT 56:4 instance is subordinated by a preceding conjunction rather than standing verse-initial. Splice both runs. TEST (the check that killed the original): collate each spliced run against the other verse and record the returned tier verbatim.
